summary: Thich Nhat Hanh was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied and taught at both Columbia and Princeton universities from 1961 to 1963, and founded the An Quang Pagoda and the School of Youth for Social Service.
Thich Thien Nghiem is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Delhi under the doctoral supervision of Shalini Singhal (attested 2012).

Thierry Mathou is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at EDHEC Business School (~1982–1985) and the Paris Institute of Political Studies (~1985–1987), and served as an Associated Political Scientist at the CNRS.

Thierry Meynard works in Sinology and philosophy. He completed a PhD in philosophy at Peking University under Yulie Lou (~1999–2003), became Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University (~2006), and directed The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies (2012).

Thinh Canh Quang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of the West (attested 2007) under supervisor Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya, having also studied under Lewis Lancaster and Ananda W. P. Guruge.

Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, and Chief Editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1994).

Thomas A. Forsthoefel is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He earned a BA at Georgetown, an MA at Loyola University Chicago, and a PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths, later serving at Mercyhurst University.

Thomas A. Tweed is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Stanford (~1979–1984) and was supervised by William R. Hutchison. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at UNC Chapel Hill (~1993–2008).

Thomas Borchert works in Buddhist and religious studies. A former PhD candidate at the University of Chicago (attested 2005), he held an appointment as Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont (attested 2017).

Thomas Burrow was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Queen Elizabeth School and Christ's College, Cambridge, he served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Oxford from around 1944 to 1976.
Thomas Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Harvard University under E. Bruce Brooks.
Thomas E. Crow is a historian and archaeologist who studied at Pomona College (~1965–1969). He later held posts at the University of Michigan (~1990–1996) and New York University (~2007).

Thomas Edward Colebrooke was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Eton College and East India Company College. He served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

Thomas Freeman Yarnall works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Washington and completed a PhD at Columbia under Robert A. F. Thurman (-2003), where he became Executive Editor in the Department of Religion.

Thomas H. Doctor is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling, completed an MA under Christian K. Wedemeyer, and conducted doctoral research at the University of Lausanne supervised by Tom J. F. Tillemans.

Thomas James Mazanec is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Calvin University and earned an MA at the University of Colorado Boulder, completing his doctoral work under Anna M. Shields, Stephen F. Teiser, and Wang Ping.

Thomas Jülch is a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2005–2011). He later served as a research fellow at Ghent University (~2015–2021).

Thomas Nathan Patton works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Cornell University, where he studied under Anne M. Blackburn, and held a post at the City University of Hong Kong (attested 2018).
Thomas Oberlies is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Albrecht Wezler. He held an academic post at the University of Freiburg (attested 2001).

Thomas P. Kasulis is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He held posts at Ashland University (~1980–1991) and Ohio State University, where he was a professor from around 1991 to 2014.
